title: Request adapter schema + fallback catalogue (working draft)
content:
Purpose
---
This doc captures a working proposal for a compact, implementation-friendly request adapter schema plus a catalog of graceful fallback behaviors that the runtime can use to preserve availability and headroom when the preferred model/kernel/instance is unavailable. It focuses on: request surface, minimal compatibility guarantees across versions, error taxonomy intended for programmatic retry/fallback decisions, and a concise KV-cache contract tied to fallbacks and scheduling hints.

Audience
- Serving runtime engineers (scheduler, kernels, kv-cache)
- SDK authors (client-side adapter layer)
- Solutions/SEs building deterministic fallbacks into customer deployments

Scope and non-goals\- Scope: schema-level primitives that upstream clients (SDKs, proxies) should send, and how the runtime interprets them for routing, kernels, and KV cache behavior. Includes examples and a fallback catalog.
- Non-goal: final wire-level protobuf types for public API (that's a follow-up); deep implementation details of allocator or kernel micro-ops.

High-level rules (design constraints)
1) Be conservative with required fields — aim for forward/backward compatibility with simple heuristics.
2) Encourage explicit hints rather than implicit behavior (e.g., client provides "kv_cache_intent" vs runtime guessing).
3) Errors must be actionable: classify into retryable transient, retryable with backoff, deterministic failure, and graceful-degrade-able.
4) Fallback catalogs must be composable and limited in policy surface.

Request adapter schema (proposal) — flat envelope for compatibility\- Envelope-level fields (top-level strings/ints/bools; no nested objects expected by runtime core):
  client_agent: string     # SDK name+version: e.g. "rnw-sdk/0.12.1"
  client_protocol_version: string  # semantic version for adapter contract e.g. "2024-09"
  request_id: string
  model_hint: string      # preferred model id (e.g. "redwood-v1-like-fp16")
  model_slo: string       # e.g., "latency:low" | "cost:low" | "balanced" (informational)
  task: string            # "text-generation" | "chat" | "embed" | "rerank"
  input_type: string      # "single" | "batched"
  input_payload: string   # opaque; raw text or concatenated for batched; SDKs must escape separators
  max_tokens: integer
  stream: boolean
  priority: integer       # 0..100, default 50; scheduler uses this
  deadline_ms: integer    # client deadline from now; runtime may use for preemption
  estimated_tokens: integer # hint for batching + scheduler; optional but strongly recommended
  kv_cache_intent: string # "none" | "use" | "fill"  (explicit cache usage intent)
  kv_cache_scope: string  # "session" | "prefix:<string>" | "opaque-key" (helps eviction semantics)
  kernel_hint: string     # "fp16" | "int8" | "prefetch-cache" | "sharded-kv" (advice to kernel/selection)
  fallback_policy: string # "none" | "model-variant" | "quantized-variant" | "region-fallback" | "degrade-response"
  accept_partial: boolean # allows returned tokens/chunks from fallback path instead of hard failure
  auth_token: string      # opaque token; not interpreted here but must be present for gate

Notes on schema: keep everything flat. The SDK must include client_protocol_version and client_agent. Runtime may ignore unknown fields for forward compatibility.

Compatibility guarantees (runtime promises)
1) Backward-compatible request acceptance: If the runtime sees a missing field (e.g., kernel_hint), it must assume a conservative default (no special kernel preference, kv_cache_intent="use" if session present).
2) Forward-compatibility: Runtime must ignore unknown enum strings and map them to a closest known value, logging a metric.
3) Stable error surface: error codes (see taxonomy) will remain stable; new codes appended but mapping levels (retryable/deterministic) must not flip.
4) Envelope version negotiation: If client_protocol_version major changes, runtime may return a MUST_UPGRADE error recommending SDK upgrade; minor/patch changes are handled by best-effort mapping.

Error taxonomy (codes and semantics) — for programmatic handling\- Level 1: Transient/retryable (client should retry with backoff)\  RTE-1000 TRANSIENT_CAPACITY_PRESSURE  # scheduler overloaded, retry with jitter\  RTE-1001 TRANSIENT_KERNEL_BUSY        # busy on kernel; short retry\  RTE-1002 TRANSIENT_REGION_UNAVAILABLE # regional outage; attempt region-fallback if allowed
\- Level 2: Retryable but requires change in request or fallback\  RTE-2000 MODEL_UNAVAILABLE            # requested model not hosted; candidate fallback: model-variant or quantized\  RTE-2001 KVCACHE_MISS_STALE           # cache missing / stale but request can proceed without it\  RTE-2002 KERNEL_INCOMPATIBLE_HINT     # requested kernel_hint cannot be honored; runtime will choose fallback kernel or return INFO+error
\- Level 3: Deterministic/consumer-fix required\  RTE-3000 MALFORMED_ENVELOPE           # client payload malformed; do not retry until fixed\  RTE-3001 AUTH_INVALID                  # token invalid/expired; client must refresh credentials
\- Level 4: Graceful degrade (return partial)\  RTE-4000 FALLBACK_PARTIAL_OUTPUT      # runtime returns partial text/embedding with warning; client can accept or retry

Each error should carry: code (above), human_message (string), suggested_actions (list of strings). The runtime JSON error body is allowed but not required here; SDKs should surface suggested_actions to users.

Fallback catalogue (ordered preference semantics)\- Policy guidance: runtime selects the first available option in the declared fallback_policy chain. SDKs can request explicit chain by adding fallback_preference header (comma-separated). If fallback_policy is "model-variant" runtime will try: 1) same-arch smaller-quantized variant 2) lower-SLO variant (e.g. latency:balanced) 3) regional replica
\- Quantized variants: marked as tolerant to deterministic differences in output quality (client should know this may change tokenization).
\- Degrade-response: return truncated or simplified response (e.g., fallback to summary or an embedding) when generation costs are prohibitive.

KV-cache contract (semantics that caller & kernel must rely on)\- Keys: opaque strings, runtime allows "prefix:" semantics supplied by client for eviction grouping. Keys must be unique per session+model.
\- TTL semantics: client can send ttl_ms hint (not authoritative). Runtime may evict earlier under memory pressure, but must emit KVCACHE_EVICT notifications in trace logs for observability.
\- Cache coherence: no cross-model reuse of KV entries unless model family is explicitly compatible and runtime announces compatibility in model metadata.
\- On fallback (quantized/model-variant), runtime is allowed to invalidate session-level KV cache if variant is incompatible. Incompatibility should generate KVCACHE_INVALIDATED warning for client.

Scheduler hints + expected runtime behaviors\- estimated_tokens and priority drive batching windows: low-estimated + high-priority -> tight batching into low-latency fast path. Large estimated_tokens -> may be routed to slower throughput-optimized nodes.
\- deadline_ms strictly respected by preemption: runtime will prefer returning partial (RTE-4000) vs missing deadline.

Examples (pseudo-envelopes)
1) Low-latency chat request{\
  client_agent: "rnw-js/0.9.3",\
  client_protocol_version: "2024-09",\
  request_id: "req-3748",\
  model_hint: "redwood-chat-v1",\
  task: "chat",\
  input_type: "single",\
  input_payload: "User: what's the ETA?\nAssistant:",\
  stream: true,\
  max_tokens: 64,\
  priority: 80,\
  deadline_ms: 1200,\
  kv_cache_intent: "use",\
  kv_cache_scope: "session",\
  fallback_policy: "model-variant,region-fallback",\
  accept_partial: true\
}

2) Bulk embed job (tolerant to quantization){\
  client_agent: "rnw-python/0.12.0",\
  client_protocol_version: "2024-09",\
  request_id: "bulk-198",\
  model_hint: "embed-large-v2",\
  task: "embed",\
  input_type: "batched",\
  input_payload: "s1\n--SPLIT--\ns2\n--SPLIT--\ns3",\
  stream: false,\
  max_tokens: 1,\
  priority: 30,\
  estimated_tokens: 6000,\
  kv_cache_intent: "none",\
  kernel_hint: "int8",\
  fallback_policy: "quantized-variant",\
  accept_partial: false\
}

Open questions / TODOs\- Decide canonical header name for fallback_preference (HTTP header vs envelope field).\- Define signal channel for KVCACHE_EVICT/KVCACHE_INVALIDATED (structured trace event vs special error code).\- Map this flat envelope to a protobuf wrapper for the public API.

Appendix: quick migration guidance for SDKs\- Always send client_protocol_version and client_agent.\- Provide estimated_tokens when possible; it materially improves scheduling.\- Explicitly set kv_cache_intent; prefer "use" for session-based chat.
